abstract: Public mouse brain single-cell and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (sc/snRNA-seq) datasets are difficult to reuse across studies because sample annotations are heterogeneous and incomplete. We harmonized sample-level metadata for 2,005 cortex and hippocampus samples from 389 studies, covering wild-type (WT) controls and Alzheimer's disease (AD)-related mouse models. Usable count data from 1,863 samples in 360 studies were uniformly processed into 12,628,942 cell and nuclear profiles with cell-type annotations. Expression-based indicators were consistent with the annotated sequencing protocol and sex, and integrated microglial profiles recovered established AD-associated signatures. To illustrate cross-study use, we asked whether microglial AD--WT expression differences varied with age and between cortex and hippocampus, using covariate-adjusted expression reconstructed with Kanade. Genes separated into groups with predominantly negative or positive AD--WT contrasts, including a group whose age-associated contrasts differed between cortex and hippocampus. These findings demonstrate the utility of harmonized metadata for investigating age- and region-dependent AD-associated transcriptional differences across studies. The resource supports explicit, reproducible cohort definitions across public mouse brain datasets.
